Advantages: FastAI-native baseline; cheap enough for repeated Kaggle runs; strong ecosystem support; easy to fine-tune
Weaknesses: Older CNN; may underperform stronger backbones on subtle diffusion artifacts
Explainability Support: Strong Grad-CAM/CAM support; residual blocks are inspection-friendly
Generalization: Strong literature support for cross-dataset benchmarking, though not diffusion-specific alone
Notes: Rank 1. Recommended baseline shortlist. Best first EXP candidate because it is reproducible, cheap, and comparable.

Advantages: Canonical deepfake baseline in the literature; depthwise separable convolutions often work well on manipulation artifacts; still Kaggle-feasible
Weaknesses: Less natural in FastAI than torchvision backbones; larger 299 input increases training cost; may be brittle across unseen generators
Explainability Support: Strong Grad-CAM support; widely used in explainability studies
Generalization: Good historical deepfake evidence; newer diffusion-era evidence is promising but still limited
Notes: Rank 2. Recommended baseline shortlist. Include as the deepfake-standard comparator.

Advantages: Strong accuracy/efficiency tradeoff; recent face-specific GAN-vs-diffusion paper includes it; mature timm support
Weaknesses: Higher input resolution raises memory/time cost; can be sensitive to preprocessing mismatch
Explainability Support: Good Grad-CAM support; MBConv blocks are still tractable to inspect
Generalization: Mixed but relevant: recent evidence on both GAN and diffusion faces, yet bias sensitivity was observed
Notes: Rank 3. Recommended baseline shortlist. Good stronger CNN once the cheap baseline is stable.

Advantages: Patch-based modeling may capture generator artifacts missed by CNNs; transformer family is explicitly present in the literature; useful architecture contrast
Weaknesses: Highest compute burden in shortlist candidates; more data-hungry; explainability is less intuitive than CNN saliency
Explainability Support: Moderate: attention rollout and Grad-CAM variants exist, but interpretation is weaker than CNNs
Generalization: Promising cross-generator relevance, but evidence is less mature and training cost is higher
Notes: Rank 4. Reserve as a transformer comparator after CNN baselines.

Advantages: Backbone used in hierarchical GAN-vs-diffusion/source-attribution literature; robust residual baseline with strong tooling
Weaknesses: Heavier than ResNet-50 without guaranteed early baseline payoff; slower Kaggle iteration
Generalization: Strong relevance to multi-generator and source-attribution literature
Notes: Rank 5. Keep as an extension candidate if ResNet-50 underfits or source-attribution work starts early.

Advantages: Parameter-efficient CNN with dense feature reuse; simple FastAI integration; cheap enough for ablations
Weaknesses: Older literature support; fewer face-forensics papers use it as the main reference today
Generalization: Limited direct evidence on diffusion-era generalization
Notes: Rank 6. Backup lightweight CNN if memory or throughput becomes a bottleneck.

Advantages: Face-specific local/global inductive bias and physiologically interpretable branch make it attractive for forensic analysis
Weaknesses: Custom architecture adds implementation risk; weaker public replication story; GAN-focused evaluation only
Explainability Support: Strong physiological explanation story around iris/pupil cues
Generalization: Limited; evaluated on narrower GAN settings, not robustly on diffusion datasets
Notes: Rank 7. Do not use as the first baseline. Consider later if explainability becomes the priority.
